gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per watt-hour or energy per pound for these D cells. From the makers' own US store prices and cell weights: Tenergy Premium D 10,000 mAh costs $0.77 per rated Wh at 33.6 Wh/lb. Tenergy Centura 8,000 mAh, ChatGPT's 'best overall', costs $0.91/Wh at 30.0 Wh/lb. Powerex costs $1.66 per guaranteed Wh at Maha's list price. EBL rates its cell at 10,000 mAh in a 126 g cell (43 Wh/lb), which takes 29% more mAh per gram than Tenergy's own 162 g 10,000 mAh cell. A BudgetLightForum tester measured EBL D cells at 6,500–7,000 mAh, which would push EBL's 4-pack to $1.19–1.28/Wh.
standout_why: I read the three cited pages. New World Survival (2026-09-01) gives rated mAh, the 85% one-year retention claim and rough 4-pack price ranges ($15–24). It reports no measured capacity, no weights and no cost per Wh, and says independent checks of EBL's claims are limited. Reactual (2023) gives rated mAh and old prices, but no weights, Wh or cost per Wh. The SFA 2016 PDF would not extract. ChatGPT's two answers repeat rated mAh and call EBL 'best value'. Neither works out cost per guaranteed or measured Wh, and neither uses cell weight to test whether a capacity claim is believable.
decides: It changes the value pick. Per rated Wh at the maker's own store, Tenergy Premium D 10,000 mAh ($36.99 for 4, $0.77/Wh) beats Centura ($0.91/Wh). It also beats EBL's retail 4-pack ($0.83/Wh). EBL's separate 'D2' 4-count at $28.88 works out to $0.60/Wh on paper. But EBL's 126 g cell weight and a named forum test (6,500–7,000 mAh) suggest its 10,000 mAh rating is inflated, so its real cost is about $1.19–1.28/Wh. Centura stays the storage pick because of its retention claim, but it costs 18% more per Wh than Tenergy Premium. Powerex is the only candidate with a published guaranteed minimum (9,000 mAh), and at $1.66 per guaranteed Wh it is the premium choice, not a value one.
